searchText: Hi all, another question. While decoding individual storage node rlps, I very rarely run across a node that fails to decode into [][]byte or []interface{}. When decoding into []byte these nodes will immediately throw an “rlp: expected input string or byte for []uint8, decoding into ([][]uint8)[14]”. When decoding into []interface{} the initial decoding works, but then when I iterate over the elements and type assert them to []byte (as is done here https://github.com/ipfs/go-ipld-eth/blob/master/trie_node.go#L127) I get a panic: "panic: interface conversion: interface {} is []interface {}, not []uint8" Upon closer inspection I can see that this is because one of the elements of the branch node does not decode into a single byte array, but instead an array of byte arrays. Specifically, for example, at block 10041344 the storage branch node at path 0b000f060b0f0700 for the state account at leafkey 0x0f27a427a06c148ea9a08f515db9ba0cdcfc7260580a2e512385db59487acd14 I am unable to decode the branch node element at position 14 into []byte, the actual value is a byte array: [[54 67 156 56 255 153 112 176 185 21 62 239 27 79 212 212 90 175 240 252 0 192 203 46 180 91 154 233] [1]] <@!211091239112671234> any insight into the above two questions would be much appreciated! > Upon closer inspection I can see that this is because one of the elements of the branch node does not decode into a single byte array, but instead an array of byte arrays. if a child's bytelength is smaller than 32, instead of the hash the node itself is embedded in the parent Thank you <@!259648573401071617> ! Is there a way you would recommend handling this when attempting to "generically" decode all nodes? 'genericaly' this is needed.. however, if you write a trie for only the main account trie, then you don't need to bother with it. For storage tries, it's required, though Martin can correct me, but i think this is the relevant part in geth: https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/blob/master/trie/node.go#L186 Thank you both! While I have your attention could I get some help with my above EIP-158 question- when an account is removed, if its leaf node was previously referenced in a branch node element- I assume that reference reverts to an empty []byte not crypto.Keccak256(rlp.EncodeToBytes([]byte{}))? afaik eip-158 doesn't change trie logic, so removing an empty account is equivalent to removing an item from the trie. So the branch child should become empty []byte Great, thank you <@!259648573401071617> , that makes sense!

excerpts.author: iannorden
excerpts.content:
Hi all, another question. While decoding individual storage node rlps, I very rarely run across a node
that fails to decode into [][]byte or []interface{}. 

When decoding into []byte these nodes will immediately throw an “rlp: expected input string or byte for []uint8, decoding into ([][]uint8)[14]”.

When decoding into []interface{} the initial decoding works, but then when I iterate over the elements and type assert them to []byte (as is done here https://github.com/ipfs/go-ipld-eth/blob/master/trie_node.go#L127) I get a panic: "panic: interface conversion: interface {} is []interface {}, not []uint8"

Upon closer inspection I can see that this is because one of the elements of the branch node does not decode into a single byte array, but instead an array of byte arrays.

Specifically, for example, at block 10041344 the storage branch node at path 0b000f060b0f0700 for the state account at leafkey 0x0f27a427a06c148ea9a08f515db9ba0cdcfc7260580a2e512385db59487acd14 I am unable to decode the branch node element at position 14 into []byte, the actual value is a byte array: [[54 67 156 56 255 153 112 176 185 21 62 239 27 79 212 212 90 175 240 252 0 192 203 46 180 91 154 233] [1]]

<@!211091239112671234> any insight into the above two questions would be much appreciated!

excerpts.author: s1na
excerpts.content:
> Upon closer inspection I can see that this is because one of the elements of the branch node does not decode into a single byte array, but instead an array of byte arrays.

if a child's bytelength is smaller than 32, instead of the hash the node itself is embedded in the parent

excerpts.author: iannorden
excerpts.content: Is there a way you would recommend handling this when attempting to "generically" decode all nodes?

excerpts.author: holiman
excerpts.content: 'genericaly' this is needed.. however, if you write a trie for only the main account trie, then you don't need to bother with it. For storage tries, it's required, though

excerpts.content: afaik eip-158 doesn't change trie logic, so removing an empty account is equivalent to removing an item from the trie. So the branch child should become empty []byte
